introduction.title: Guide to Setting Up Excel Files
introduction.content: This guide is designed to help researchers set up their own node connections, node attributes, and system settings for use in the simulation environment. The setup involves creating three Excel files: one for defining the connections between nodes and their corresponding influence factors, another for specifying node attributes such as alignment, and a third for setting system parameters for the red and blue teams. This guide provides step-by-step instructions on how to format these files, what each column represents, and how to ensure compatibility with the simulation system.

overview.title: Overview
overview.content: The Node Connections file defines how each node in the network is connected to other nodes and the strength of those connections (influence factors). This file should be saved as an Excel file with the sheet named 'NodeConnections'.

structure.title: File Structure
tableContent: The unique identifier for each node in the network.
A comma-separated list of nodes directly connected to the node in the first column.
A comma-separated list of influence factors corresponding to each connected node.

instructions.title: Instructions
content: Open Excel and create a new workbook. This workbook must have the exact same layout and titles as provided in the example excel files.
Enter the data as shown in the example, ensuring that each node's connections and influence factors are correctly listed.
Save the file and upload it by following the standard importing process.

tips.title: Tips
content: Ensure that the 'Connected_Nodes' and 'Influence_Factor' columns have matching numbers of entries, separated by commas.
The influence factor should be a value between 0.2 and 0.5, where a higher value indicates a stronger influence.

overview.title: Overview
overview.content: The Node Attributes file defines the properties of each node, such as alignment. This file should be saved as an Excel file with the sheet named 'NodeAttributes'.

structure.title: File Structure
tableContent: The unique identifier for each node, consistent with the 'Node' column in the Node Connections file.
A value representing the initial alignment of the node.

content.description: Represents a Red alignment, indicating the node is inclined towards the Red side.
Represents a Neutral alignment, indicating the node does not strongly favor either side.
Represents a Blue alignment, indicating the node is inclined towards the Blue side.

instructions.title: Instructions
content: Open Excel and create a new workbook. This workbook must have the exact same layout and titles as provided in the example excel files.
Enter the data as shown in the example, ensuring that each node's attributes are correctly listed.
Save the file and upload it by following the standard importing process.

tips.title: Tips
content: Ensure that the 'Node_ID' in this file matches the 'Node' identifiers in the Node Connections file.
The 'Alignment' values should all be between `alignment_max` and `alignment_min`.

overview.title: Overview
overview.content: The simulation settings file defines parameters for the red and blue teams. It specifies LLMs for both the red and blue teams, and the necessary parameters which influence how the models play in the simulation. It is important to note that models specified in this file must be already connected to the simulation system.

structure.title: File Structure: Settings for Agents
tableContent: The colour identifier of the team that the settings are for. The first row must specifiy settings for the red agent, and the second row must specify settings for the blue agent. There must only be one 'Red' agent and one 'Blue' agent.
The unique identifier for each LLM connected to the simulation. If using a custom LLM, enter 'custom'.

A whole number between 1 and 100 (inclusive) representing the initial energy levels of the blue team only (any input for the red team is discarded as the red team has infinite energy). This value depletes after every turn the blue team takes, depending on the message’s energy cost.
A whole number between 1 and 10 (inclusive) which dictates the number of messages at different potency levels the model generates per turn.

A value between 0 and 1 that determines how random or predictable the model’s output should be. A lower temperature will result in more deterministic output whereas higher values like 0.8 will result in more random output.
A value between 0 and 1 that represents the influence the team has over other nodes in the simulation.
An integer value that represents the maximum cost a message can have.
A percentage value (between 0 to 100 inclusive) applied to the potency of the message when it exceeds a certain threshold.

A value between 0 to 100 (inclusive) which determines when the penalty is applied to the potency of a red team message. If the potency of a message exceeds this threshold, a penalty (set as a percentage) is applied to reduce the potency.

energyExplanation.title: 'Energy' Explanation
energyExplanation.content: The Energy value represents how much 'energy' the blue team begins with. This can be thought of as the resources available to the blue team. Upon each turn, the blue team generates messages of varying potency levels and assigns an 'energy cost' to each one. The blue team’s overall energy level decreases by the energy cost of a message sent out to the simulation on a given turn. The red team does not have an energy level, as they are acting with 'unlimited resources'.

msgsGeneratedExplanation.title: 'Msgs_Generated' Explanation
msgsGeneratedExplanation.content: The Msgs_Generated value specifies how many messages a model should generate on their turn. Each message will be of a different potency level, ranging from low to high potency. For example, if Msgs_Generated is set to 3, the model will generate three messages: one low potency message, one medium potency message, and one high potency message. The minimum value is 1 and the maximum is 10.

temperatureExplanation.title: 'Temperature' Explanation
temperatureExplanation.content: The Temperature value determines how random or predictable the model’s output should be: Low temperature (0.0 to 0.25): more deterministic and predictable output. Neutral temperature (0.5): balanced output. High temperature (0.75 to 1.0): more random and non-deterministic output.

penaltyExplaination.title: 'Penalty' Explanation
penaltyExplaination.content: The penalty value represents a reduction in the potency of the red team’s messages when they exceed a certain potency threshold. This threshold acts as a limit, beyond which the potency of a message is penalised. The penalty is applied as a percentage reduction of the message's potency. For each turn, if a red team message surpasses the potency threshold, the penalty is calculated as a percentage of the potency, and is then subtracted from the original potency, hence reducing its effectiveness in the simulation. The blue team does not have a penalty.

instructions.title: Instructions
content: Open Excel and create a new workbook. This workbook must have the exact same layout and titles as provided in the example excel files.
Enter the data as shown in the example, ensuring that each parameter is correctly entered and is within the correct range.
Save the file and upload it by following the standard importing process.

structure.title: File Structure: Settings for Custom Termination Conditions
tableContent: A percentage value between 0 to 100 (inclusive) which defines the population percentage required for either the red or blue team to win. Once a team reaches this percentage of alignment, the simulation ends.

A whole number between 0 and 50 (inclusive) which sets a limit on the maximum number of rounds the simulation can run for. The simulation will terminate once this number of rounds is reached, regardless of the population alignments.

importingFiles.title: Importing Parameters from Excel Files
steps: Navigate to the Home page and select 'Upload Excel Files'.

Upload all three required Excel files (NodeConnections, NodeAttributes, and SimulationSettings) one at a time by clicking 'Choose file' for each file. When prompted, select the file you wish to upload and click 'open'.

Once you have selected all three files, proceed to upload them by clicking 'Upload Files'. If successful, you will be redirected to confirm the imported values are correct. If an error occurs, please check the file formatting and entered values are correct.
If necessary, adjust the files and re-upload them by going back to the 'Home' page.
Run the simulation after confirming all data is correctly imported.

parameterInstructions.title: Instructions
parameterInstructions.overview: The simulation can be run with either default or customised parameters. Parameters can be set either through the UI or by uploading excel files.
defaultSteps: On the Home page, click “Enter Parameters”.
Select “Random” from the drop down menu for the Green Node Configuration.
Click “Next” to then either choose to run the simulation continuously (without user input) or in turns (where the simulation requires the user to click “next turn” to progress to the next round).
uiSteps: On the Home page, click “Enter Parameters”.
Select desired values for both the red and blue agents (if running with a custom LLM, see the “Custom LLM Guide” below).
Select “User Input” from the drop down menu for the Green Node Configuration and select desired values for the green network/population.
Click “Next” to then either choose to run the simulation continuously (without user input) or in turns (where the simulation requires the user to click “next turn” to progress to the next round).

errors.Error occurred when importing files: Iss: This occurs when the file uploaded for simulation settings has incorrect formatting. The error message may be followed by something along the lines of 'Model_ID' or 'Alignment', which indicates there may be a missing column for that parameter. Please ensure that the excel files have the exact same formatting and titles as the provided example files.
errors.Error occurred when importing files: inv: This occurs when the file uploaded contains invalid values for the specified parameter. Please ensure that all required parameters are provided and all entered values are of the correct type and within the specified ranges (see above).
